response.query: Provide studies relevant to: Homogeneity of corporate risk perceptions and systemic financial risk, topics discussed:
response.answer: Homogeneity in corporate risk perceptions can amplify systemic financial risk, as uniform misperceptions can lead to synchronized risk-taking. Studies show that diverse risk assessments can mitigate systemic risk, highlighting the importance of varied corporate risk views. Research indicates that systemic risk is often underestimated in corporate risk management.

results.title: The Zero Lower Bound Remains a Medium-Term Risk
results.content: Line chart tracking baseline estimated probability distribution of short-term interest rates (gold) and two hypothetical distributions for lower expected level of interest rates (blue) and higher uncertainty (red) by density (y-axis axis) and percent (x-axis); zero lower bound (ZLB) is marked by a vertical line, dashed lines represent negative interest rates; the hypothetical distributions are calibrated such that they imply the same ZLB risk, demonstrating that ZLB risk rises with either a decrease in the expected level of interest rates or an increase in uncertainty. Line chart tracking the seven-year ahead zero lower bound (ZLB) risk (gold, right axis), expected level of interest rates (blue, left axis), and uncertainty (red, left axis) by percent (vertical axis) from 2007 through 2025 (horizontal axis); current seven-year ahead ZLB risk is comparable to 2018, even though the expected interest rate is higher, reflecting that uncertainty is higher now than in 2018. The next chart shows the term structures of ZLB risk, the expected level of interest rates, and uncertainty across forecast horizons ranging from 2 to 10 years, reported on May 27, 2025.
